claims.statement: The repository deploys a root Next.js marketplace and a separately configured MCP Express service; the MCP Vercel deployment builds independently and rewrites all paths to an Express-function entrypoint.
The web service-role Supabase client is server-only, refuses creation when `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` is absent, and disables persisted/refreshing auth sessions.
The MCP service exits on missing Supabase URL or service-role key, keeps that credential server-side, and exposes partners only to separately validated `i24_` Bearer tokens.

MCP write capability is rollout-gated by the comma-separated `MCP_WRITE_ENABLED` configuration, while a nonempty `ALLOWED_HOSTS` list enables DNS-rebinding protection for its stateless Streamable HTTP transport.

The root Next configuration applies HSTS, MIME-type, framing, referrer, permissions, and CSP headers to every route; the CSP permits browser connectivity to the site, Supabase, and Sentry and currently retains inline script/style allowances.
The web configuration preserves the externally registered `/webhooks/uber-direct` endpoint by rewriting it to `/api/webhooks/uber-direct`.

Sentry initializes before client hydration with PII disabled, configurable trace/replay sampling, masked replay text/media, feedback integration, and router-transition breadcrumbs; server instrumentation selects distinct Node or Edge initialization based on `NEXT_RUNTIME` and registers request-error capture.
The generic API error helper captures the actual exception in Sentry but returns a generic response, preventing database/provider error messages from being exposed to callers.
Vercel schedules daily `GET /api/carrinho/abandono/tick`; its GET path requires `CRON_SECRET`, while its manual/alternate POST path requires `ASAAS_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, and both route into the same scan.

The abandoned-cart tick requires service-role availability, selects carts idle at least an hour without a reminder marker, marks a cart reminded only after email success, treats WhatsApp as supplementary, and reports success, alert, or failure outcomes.

`POST /api/coletivas/tick` has no repository-managed scheduler and requires the Asaas webhook Bearer token plus service-role configuration; it runs collective stages and returns recorded success or failure outcomes.

The central event writer records bounded capability/origin/result records and optional reason/metadata in `observabilidade_eventos`, but missing service configuration, insertion failures, and exceptions are logged and absorbed so observability cannot cause its caller to reject.
The observability-event table is RLS-enabled with no policies, indexed by capability and descending creation time, and is intended to be read and written only through service-role code.

The cron-history endpoint requires `CRON_SECRET` and service-role configuration, returns up to 50 newest cron events grouped by origin with a latest record and up to ten history records, and sends query errors through the generic Sentry-reporting error response.
The dashboard-ops deployment proxies the protected cron-history endpoint using its own `CRON_SECRET`; missing local configuration returns 500 and an unavailable/error upstream returns 502.

The Uber webhook only rejects a bad signature when its signing key is configured; with a configured key it HMAC-validates `x-uber-signature`, captures invalid signatures as Sentry warnings, and responds 401.

The separate dashboard-ops Vercel deployment schedules daily `GET /api/push-metrics`; that route gathers its GitHub, Vercel, and Sentry dashboard data and pushes numeric metrics to the configured Prometheus remote-write endpoint, reporting a non-200/204 push as 502.
The dashboard polls GitHub, Vercel, Sentry, and cron APIs every 30 seconds and presents cron latest-status/timestamp information alongside unresolved Sentry issues and transaction-latency summaries.

Dashboard provider routes independently retrieve GitHub, Vercel, and Sentry data with server-side credentials and return local JSON errors on provider failure; Sentry keeps issue data when its optional latency request fails.
The dashboard metrics-push route has no application-level authorization check and uses `GRAFANA_PRHOMOTEUS_API_KEY` as its remote-write password.
Sentry user context contains only a user ID and optional role, avoiding email and other PII.
